patient_information: A 22-year-old woman from Ashulia near Dhaka, Bangladesh, who recently visited a religious festival.
chief_complaint: Passing 12 to 15 large-volume stools in the past day and becoming unresponsive.
history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced passing 12 to 15 large-volume, rice-water stools with white flakes in the past day, became unresponsive about an hour prior to hospital admission, and did not complain of pain or fever.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient attended a religious festival where water was supplied in large metal containers, and her husband reported that five or six other attendees were also ill with diarrhoea; 44 additional cases of cholera were identified by local health authorities.
vitals: Pulse rate 110 bpm (low volume), blood pressure 90/50 mmHg, afebrile.
physical_exam: Stuporous, minimally responsive to painful stimuli (GCS 9/15), afebrile, with sunken eyes, dry mouth, scaphoid abdomen, and very slow skin pinch return.
labs_and_diagnostics: Laboratory results showed sodium 143.8 mmol/L, potassium 3.0 mmol/L, chloride 103.8 mmol/L, bicarbonate 11.4 mmol/L, lactic acid (venous) 4.1 mmol/L, creatine 203 µmol/L, and blood urea nitrogen 8.6 mmol/L; stool examination revealed liquid, rice-water appearance with no faecal matter, small slender curved bacilli with darting motility inhibited by Vibrio cholerae antiserum O1, and culture growing V. cholerae O1, Serotype Ogawa, biotype El Tor.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was immediately started on intravenous rehydration with Ringer's lactate solution; after 3 L in the first hour, pulse rate and blood pressure improved to 84 bpm and 100/70 mmHg; an additional 2 L were given over the next 3 hours, after which she became alert and responsive; she was then started on oral rehydration and given a single dose of 300 mg doxycycline, and was discharged on the third day when stool consistency had returned to normal.
